conviction_note: Q3 revenue, EBITDA and EBITA were released by ad-hoc on 2026-10-26, along with a cut to the revenue guide and a confirmed EBITDA/EBITA guide. The stock fell 6% on that ad-hoc and another 2.8% since. What 12 Nov adds is Q4 commentary, the 9M cash flow and possibly a note on where in the ranges the year lands. The findings offset: the low end needs a Q4 that beats Q3's run-rate (small negative); Bechtle's strong Q4 read-across and an ongoing buyback taking ~25-30% of volume are small positives. p_up stays at 50 and abs_move sits at the pre-released / guide-reiterated scale, lifted slightly for a 6.2% disclosed short and 37% realised vol.

already_public.what: Preliminary Q3 2026: revenue ~EUR 412.0m (Q3.25 423.9m), EBITDA EUR 24.1m (27.1m), EBITA ~EUR 10.8m (13.4m). FY26 revenue guide cut to EUR 1,650-1,750m (from 1,750-1,850m). EBITDA 110-130m and EBITA 55-75m confirmed (ad-hoc, MAR Art. 17, 26-Oct-2026 17:59 CET)
H1 2026: revenue EUR 775.9m, EBITDA 49.2m, EBITA 21.5m, operating cash flow EUR -109.6m, cash EUR 21.5m at 30 June. FY guide confirmed at the time
Buyback of up to 1,436,985 shares (5%) running 7 Sep - 31 Dec 2026. 1,099,868 bought by 6 Nov, about 27k shares/day in the week of 2-6 Nov

new_in_release.expect: The EBITDA/EBITA ranges were confirmed 17 days earlier with Q3 already known, so a change is unlikely. A 'lower end' qualifier is the likely wording, and per Jefferies (via dpa-AFX) the market already sits at the low end of EBITDA. A cut to the profit guide would be the tail risk (negative)

Q4 order intake and demand commentary, especially Workplace. Jefferies says order intake is still weak. Direction unknown; Bechtle's 'strong performance continued into Q4' is the only counterparty read and it is positive

9M operating cash flow and net debt after an H1 OCF of -109.6m, with roughly EUR 24m spent on buybacks since September. Direction unknown, and it is the line most able to surprise (see Luceco in LESSONS)
Q3 detail (gross margin, segments, services vs hardware). Pre-released, expected at the ad-hoc numbers

findings.finding: On the company's own figures, the confirmed FY26 floor needs Q4 EBITDA >= EUR 36.7m (110 - 49.2 - 24.1) against Q4.25 ~38.7m, and Q4 EBITA >= 22.7m against ~24.2m. Q3 ran -11% (EBITDA) and -19% (EBITA) year on year, and that run-rate would land FY at ~108/~52, below both floors. So the release has to show Q4 momentum or concede the bottom of the ranges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 26-Oct revenue-guide cut with profit confirmed: -6.0% close to close (22.65 -> 21.30, Yahoo tape). H1 on 11-Aug, guide confirmed but revenue weak: the baseline's estimated-date reaction is -6.24%
findings.original_quote: Am Markt hätten sich die Erwartungen bereits in der Mitte der neuen Umsatzspanne und am unteren Ende der Bandbreite für das operative Ergebnis (Ebitda) befunden, urteilte der Experte. [The expert judged that market expectations were already at the middle of the new revenue range and at the low end of the range for operating profit (EBITDA).] (dpa-AFX, 27.10.26)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Jefferies says the market already sits at the low end of EBITDA, and the stock is down ~8.6% over 20 sessions. What is not priced is a profit-guide cut below the floor, which the arithmetic makes possible but which management ruled out 17 days earlier with Q3 in hand. Q4.25 figures are derived as FY25 (102.5 / 47.8, https://finanzen.net/nachricht/aktien/eqs-news-cancom-se-business-rebound-continues-cancom-meets-2025-forecast-15483986) minus 9M25 backed out of the H1 and Q3 releases. That is inference on primary numbers, so the finding is sized small
findings.independence: Jefferies via dpa-AFX: order intake still weak (https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/nachrichten/ROUNDUP-IT-Dienstleister-Cancom-kappt-Umsatzprognose-fuer-2026---Aktie-im-Minus-a43773c6-317d-4f30-ab9a-f5dbf77de58e)

findings.finding: Direct peer Bechtle's ad-hoc of 5 Nov, after Cancom's: Q3 business volume +19%, EBT +14%, 'strong performance has continued into the fourth quarter', a record order backlog, and an EBT guide raised for the second time. That is a positive read for the DACH IT-reseller Q4 that Cancom's floor depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cancom did not respond to the read-across: 5 Nov flat at 21.20, 6 Nov -3.1% to 20.55. dpa-AFX notes Cancom is recovering more slowly than Bechtle, which raised its guide after H1 while Cancom cut
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, or rejected: Cancom fell the day after it. This is a counterparty proxy, not a Cancom number, and the divergence between the two (share gain at Bechtle, Workplace weakness at Cancom) has held all year. Kept small

findings.finding: Cancom's buyback is still running through the window: 337k of 1.437m shares remain to be bought by 31 Dec, at ~27k shares/day in the week of 2-6 Nov against ~60-150k daily XETRA volume. A known bid of a quarter or more of turnover cushions the downside on a reaction day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback was running on 27 Oct and the stock still fell 6%, so the cushion is partial
findings.why_not_priced: Public through weekly filings. Its effect is mechanical flow under safe-harbour volume limits rather than information, so the expected effect on the session is small

lessons_applied: 'Lands inside what the company already guided': the guidance finding moved -0.8 -> -0.5, because the low end it points to is what Jefferies says the market already holds
'A narrow proxy loses': the Bechtle read-across moved +0.4 -> +0.3, and the buyback +0.3 -> +0.2 because it is public, ongoing flow
'Guide reiterated -> median 2.3%, pre-released -> 3.1%': abs_move_pct moved 4.0 -> 3.5, kept above 3.1 for the 6.2% short, 37% realised vol and an unknown cash-flow line
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': the 9M cash flow is named as the line most able to surprise in new_in_release. No sourced number exists, so nothing was filed
